terms.grammar: verb, irregular; in full, in computātrum trānsferre
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.189: litterae … dē tabulīs in librōs trānsferuntur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Our choice: no reference work has a verb for scanning. Classically trānsferre is to carry something over, and also to copy writing from one book into another (Lewis & Short); scanning carries the page over into the computer.
Built on scandere, which classically means to climb, or to scan verse; the English sense of scan does not come through in Latin.

phrases.english: Scan the page into the computer.

sources: Lewis & Short: transfero · Lewis & Short: scando
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 262.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
